description: Randomized-sketch (Nystrom / HMT) low-rank splitter for shape 7 (mixed1024), which sits ~at the cuSOLVER floor: its batch is heterogeneous (a sibling measured a low-rank/structured subset + a dense remainder), so a per-matrix randomized range sketch Y=A*Omega (adaptive width from a cheap energy probe) + one power iteration + tensor-core CholeskyQR gives a dominant-subspace basis; Rayleigh-Ritz the sketched subspace and route ONLY the genuinely-dense residual matrices to cuSOLVER as one contiguous batch (avoiding the ~50ms per-call fragmentation floor a sibling measured by keeping the dense remainder a single batched call). Distinct from the earlier n=512 HMT work and from the peel path — a rank-adaptive sketch sized to shape 7's measured per-matrix numerical rank. Targets redundant-work (full n=1024 solve on reducible matrices); keep the per-matrix residual gate + cuSOLVER fallback, route guarded per shape.

t1: sketch splitter mechanism in place + shape-7 route + PROFILE + rank-distribution measurement. nsys shape 7: full-batch cuSOLVER syevd (cuds_symv 28%, gemvx 19%, sytrd4 8%, laed D&C), ~88ms GPU. EXACT per-matrix numrank (energy gate 1e-3): min/med/max 214/429/1023; <=384:9, <=608:43, <=768:49, ==n:0 of 60 -> the batch IS reducible (43/60 to rank<=608) but tail decays slowly (median 429). Sketch probe w=128 under-detects (cum[127] extrapolation bug) so it currently no-ops to whole-batch cuSOLVER = parent. 39/39 valid. shape 7 110208us (cuSOLVER floor).

t2: PR-window reducibility classifier + MEASURED economic gate. KEY MEASUREMENTS on shape 7: (1) k=608-reducible = exactly the dense-cond2 subset (28/60), razor-tight PR window [107.7,112.5], cleanly separated from all other profiles. PR classifier is free (already computed) and exactly matches ground-truth. (2) cuSOLVER cost sweep: floor ~57ms + 0.90ms/mat marginal (huge fixed floor). (3) reducible low-rank at k=608 = 1.25ms/mat, dominated by k=608 cluster reduced-eigh 0.72ms/mat (intrinsic; k>448 needs C=2 cluster kernel, single-CTA megakernel only fits k<=448 and only 2-10 mats reduce that far). ECONOMICS: split = lr(28)*1.25 + cuSOLVER(32 dense w/floor) = 120.8ms vs whole 111ms => LOSS 9.8ms. Split loses because low-rank/mat (1.25) > cuSOLVER marginal/mat (0.90) and the ~57ms floor persists as long as any dense matrix remains. Economic gate correctly no-ops (fire=False). 39/39 valid; shape 7 106739us == parent, geomean 27526us.

t3: force-fire correctness harness + END-TO-END split measurement. VALIDATED the FIRE path is correct (test.20 n=1024 mixed passes forced through the split, residuals under gate). DEFINITIVE end-to-end measurement with force-fire: shape 7 = 115920us vs no-op/parent 106730us = +9181us (+8.6%) LOSS, matching the predicted -9.8ms economic loss. Confirms shape 7 is dense-batch-bound at the cuSOLVER ~57ms fixed floor: the 28-matrix reducible dense-cond2 subset solves at 1.25ms/mat (k=608 cluster reduced-eigh 0.72ms/mat, already 2.1x faster than cuSOLVER's 43ms and irreducible) which EXCEEDS cuSOLVER's 0.90ms/mat marginal, so removing them adds more low-rank cost than the marginal cuSOLVER saving while the floor persists. Also refuted: multi-profile split (220ms, rankdef k768 100% fallback), minimal 2-way clustered peel (-3.1ms), power iters (don't move matrices to k<=448). Economic gate keeps fire=False. Clean metric 27335us (parent 27359, noise); shape 7 106730us == parent, no overhead.

Built the full randomized-sketch low-rank splitter for shape 7 (mixed1024) + profiled + measured the rank distribution and reducible-vs-dense cost split exhaustively. RESULT: shape 7 is GENUINELY DENSE-BATCH-BOUND at the cuSOLVER fixed floor -- the sketch splitter LOSES by a measured +8.6% on shape 7, so the mechanism is committed with a measured economic gate that keeps it no-oping to whole-batch cuSOLVER (no regression; clean geomean 27335us == parent 27359 within noise, shape 7 106730us == parent, zero overhead).

RANK DISTRIBUTION (shape 7, b60, n=1024): energy-tail numerical rank (gate 1e-2) min/med/max 142/286/1014, <=384:47 <=608:50 ==n:0. BUT the RESIDUAL-gate-achievable rank is far stricter (orthogonality+complement capture): only 2/60 clear at k=384, 8/60 at k=512, 36/60 at k=608, 37/60 at k=768. The 28-36 that clear at k=608 are EXACTLY the dense-cond2 profile (weight 6/15), in a razor-tight PR window [107.7,112.5] -- PR (a free eigenvalue-decay energy probe) is the measured PERFECT classifier (a wide sketch eigh would hit the same cuSOLVER floor + its CholeskyQR fails on rank-deficient members).

COST SPLIT (measured, this host): cuSOLVER cost(m) ~ 57ms FIXED FLOOR + 0.90ms/mat marginal (batch-count sweep 4->60). Reducible low-rank at k=608 = 1.25ms/mat, dominated by the k=608 cluster reduced-eigh 0.72ms/mat (already 2.1x faster than cuSOLVER's 43ms on 608x608 blocks -- IRREDUCIBLE, the single-CTA megakernel only fits k<=448 and only 2-10 mats reduce that far). Oracle split (28 reducible->low-rank 35ms + 32 dense->one cuSOLVER 80ms) = 115ms vs whole 105ms = -10ms. It loses because low-rank/mat (1.25) > cuSOLVER marginal/mat (0.90) and the ~57ms floor persists as long as any dense matrix remains: removing 28 reducibles drops cuSOLVER only 25ms while adding 35ms low-rank.

ALSO REFUTED (all measured): multi-profile split routing every profile to its best path = 220ms (rankdef k768 100% fallback = 100ms for 5 mats); minimal 2-way clustered-2level peel = -3.1ms (peeling 5 clustered costs 7ms 2-level vs 4ms cuSOLVER marginal); dense608+clustered+rest 3-way = -12.4ms; power iterations 2/3 (don't move matrices into the fast k<=448 range -- reducibility is spectral-tail-intrinsic); cheaper GEMM modes (plain-tf32 CQR slower/adds fallbacks); free_tail (negligible 1.244 vs 1.252); reduced-eigh via cuSOLVER (43ms, 2.1x slower than the 20ms cluster kernel already used); whole-batch cluster megakernel = 222ms.

OPEN directions I did NOT reach (manager's call): (1) the ENERGY-tail rank is far more optimistic (47/60 <=384) than the residual-achievable rank (2/60) -- the gap is the ORTHOGONALITY gate on the discarded complement; a solver that captures the top-384 energy AND enforces orthogonality cheaply on those 47 mats (Nystrom with an explicit near-null tail + a cheap orthonormality fix) might clear more mats at the FAST k<=448 single-CTA megakernel range (0.72->much less per mat), which is the ONLY regime that could beat the 0.90ms marginal. (2) A batched dense n=1024 tensor-core eigensolver that beats cuSOLVER's per-call floor would remove the floor entirely and make ANY split win -- the k>448 cluster path (222ms) is not it; a TMA/tcgen05 tiled tridiag->D&C is unbuilt. (3) The FIRE path is validated-correct and runtime-economic-gated, so a leaderboard reseed that shifts shape 7 toward cheaper/more-reducible matrices would auto-trigger it -- worth leaving in. Mechanism, profile, and all cost data are on the branch; parent-profile-equivalent nsys captures at profiles/2026-06-30-18-52-36-eigh/brief-106-trial-{1,2}-shape7-*.nsys-rep.
